keyFindings.description: The fourth copy of the sentence rounds 7 and 8 corrected: 'takes its holds back at its next accepted registration', where registerSession re-promotes before it issues the request (the loop at :1601-1604 precedes client.subscribe at :1606). Judged Minor and not held for: the two descriptions a maintainer reads before changing this code - the production comment at envoy.ts:615-622 and packages/pi-envoy/AGENTS.md:436 - now both state it correctly, so a test comment cannot outrank them, and the change it could invite (moving the promotion behind acceptance) costs at most one registration interval rather than a role. The reviewer's own sweep missed it, because it grepped the old hold model's phrases and not this one.

The smoke's 'accepted registrations' is an attempt ordinal, not an acceptance count: the fixture increments its counter and logs `registration <n>` before the request is issued, and last_registration reports the highest such number. With the third post wedged, a run that logs seven has had at most six accepted. Judged Minor because the arm's load-bearing observations are read from the listener rather than the fixture log - the session still listed 365 s past the wedge, and last_seen advanced - and recorded in the PR body's Not proven / risk so the permanent record is accurate rather than the script silently relabelled after the fact.
